messages:
Eileen Park: quick note — BrightNest onboarding hit a short spike of 429s after we pushed a keystore rotate at 08:30 UTC. Pattern: multiple `401` then a burst of `429` when clients retried.

Noah Rivera: are they on SPA/browser flow or server-side?

Eileen Park: SPA, ephemeral tokens. Their client refresh interval was 30s with zero jitter. Tabs firing together caused preflight fanout.

Tess (devex): common story. Can you grab a small log and the response headers? especially `x-rw-limit-remaining` and `retry-after`.

Eileen Park: log snippet: `2026-03-02T08:30:12Z WARN auth invalid_sig tok=eyJ..; 2026-03-02T08:30:12Z WARN rate 429 path=/v1/preflight x-rw-limit-remaining=0 retry-after=2`

Noah Rivera: immediate mitigation: ask customer to increase refresh to 75-120s and add jitter (0-1s). I'll ping them.

Tess (devex): KB quick fix to add: sample JS jittered refresh: `setTimeout(refresh, 60000 + Math.floor(Math.random()*1000))`. Also note to temporarily hold keystore rotations during large onboarding waves.

Eileen Park: sent change request; BrightNest moved to 90s + jitter at 08:34 UTC.

deploy-bot: TKT-4042 created: "Keystore rotation: accept old signatures for 30s after rotate + gateway burst mitigation" — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/TKT-4042

Noah Rivera: after the client change 429s dropped to baseline within a minute. Customer confirms flows are OK.

Tess (devex): follow-ups: I'll add a note in the onboarding checklist about ephemeral token fanout and link to TKT-4042. Eileen — mark this triaged?

Eileen Park: marking triaged. Will reopen if we see reoccurrence.
